title: Electrical pre-start
audience: Trainee or new worker on the window cleaning (all heights) track, working under supervision.
learningOutcomes: Inspect plugs, cables, chargers, switches and housings for defects before energising equipment.
Tag out faulty equipment and report intermittent faults rather than resetting them repeatedly.
Explain that this lesson does not authorise work on, isolation of or repair to electrical installations or solar (PV) systems.

instruction.heading: Exterior, height and access context
instruction.body: This lesson is part of the window cleaning (all heights) track. The track covers ground-level, water-fed pole and elevated access work on glazing and frames. Any work above ground level, or from a ladder, scaffold or elevating work platform, is restricted: it needs employer authorisation under a site-specific risk assessment, and the worker must hold any licence the relevant state or territory requires for the equipment used. This lesson does not grant the right to work at height or on solar systems.

instruction.heading: Instruction
instruction.body: Inspect plugs, cords, housings and safety controls; isolate defective equipment and follow site electrical rules.

instruction.heading: Learning goal and job context
instruction.body: This lesson teaches electrical pre-start for routine cleaning work. Start with the actual job scope, site instructions, manufacturer directions and worker training. Never treat a general lesson as authority to perform restricted or specialist work.

instruction.heading: Core procedure
instruction.body: Inspect plugs, cables, chargers, switches and equipment condition before energising. Observe site electrical testing and residual-current protection requirements. Never use damaged leads, overload outlets or handle electrical equipment with wet hands. Tag out faults and arrange authorised inspection.

instruction.heading: Decision-making in the field
instruction.body: Before acting, ask: What is the surface or equipment? What is the soil or hazard? Which product or method is approved? What could harm a person, property or food? If the answer is unclear, pause, protect the area and seek supervisor guidance.

instruction.heading: Guided supervised practice

instruction.heading: Stop-work rule
instruction.body: Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

instruction.heading: Electrical notice
instruction.body: Electrical notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work on, isolate or repair solar (PV) systems or any electrical installation. In Victoria, PV installation and maintenance is electrical installation work that only licensed electrical installation workers may carry out, and PV DC supply cables may still be live when the power is off. NSW electrical wiring work includes repairing. Isolation and testing in this lesson apply to portable equipment only, not to a PV system. Electrical testing, isolation and repair of PV systems need a licensed electrician; in Victoria, Energy Safe Victoria guidance supports installation, maintenance and repair by licensed electrical workers, but not testing or who may isolate. Treat all panels and cables as live, and refer any electrical fault to a licensed electrician.

procedure: Confirm the job scope and the site electrical rules before you start.
Inspect plugs, cables, chargers, switches and the equipment's condition before you switch it on.
Follow the site's electrical testing and residual-current protection requirements.
Do not use damaged leads or overloaded outlets, and do not handle electrical equipment with wet hands.
If equipment trips a breaker or a fault is intermittent, stop and report it rather than resetting it repeatedly.
Tag out faulty equipment and arrange an authorised inspection.
Leave repair to an authorised person, and do not isolate, repair or work on electrical installations or solar systems under this lesson.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Licence and height notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work at height, on roofs, from elevated work platforms, or on solar systems. Completing it is not a licence, certificate or authority for regulated work. Boom-type elevating work platforms need a high risk work licence in Victoria at any boom length, and in New South Wales, Queensland, Tasmania, the Northern Territory and Western Australia where the boom is 11 metres or more. The WorkSafe WA page (last updated 13 August 2026) and the NT WorkSafe bulletin (no date shown) both state the 11-metre threshold. Check whether this work needs a high-risk work licence with the state regulator before you start. Queensland's definition does not cover platforms under 11 metres (WorkSafe Queensland page, no date shown). Tasmania's WP licence applies where the boom length is 11 metres or more, and no licence is needed for a boom under 11 metres (WorkSafe Tasmania page, last updated 1 December 2023). In New South Wales and Queensland the boom length is 11 metres: a boom-type platform of 11 metres or more needs the licence, and a shorter boom may not need it in those states. Victoria's WP class has no boom-length threshold, so the licence is not limited by length there. This lesson does not grant a licence. Scissor lifts need no high risk work licence in Victoria or the Northern Territory. Check the licence rules for your state or territory and obtain your employer's written authorisation before any work above ground level.

Electrical testing, isolation and repair of PV systems need a licensed electrician; in Victoria, Energy Safe Victoria guidance supports installation, maintenance and repair by licensed electrical workers, but not testing or who may isolate. Treat all panels and cables as live, and refer any electrical fault to a licensed electrician.

summary: Plugs, cables, chargers, switches and housings are inspected for defects before equipment is energised.
Damaged leads, overloaded outlets and handling with wet hands are never used, and site testing and residual-current protection requirements are observed.
A faulty or intermittent machine is tagged out and reported rather than reset repeatedly, and this lesson does not authorise electrical or solar work.

knowledgeChecks.question: What should you check before performing electrical pre-start?
options: Whether the lead is taped where it is damaged and whether the tape is the right colour and the lead is still warm
Plugs, cables, chargers, switches and equipment condition before energising, with residual-current protection observed
Whether the machine has been used before and by whom, and how long ago it was used last time in the shed
Whether the power point looks clean and whether the wall socket is painted and the cover is new

knowledgeChecks.question: What do you do when a cable shows a fault during a pre-start check?
options: Stop, isolate and tag out the fault, and arrange an authorised inspection
Keep using it with dry hands and do not switch it off first
Repair the cable with electrical tape and then check it again later
Reset the breaker until the machine holds and then leave it running all day

knowledgeChecks.question: What should you do when equipment trips a breaker intermittently?
options: Stop, and report the intermittent trip rather than resetting it repeatedly
Reset the breaker and continue with the floor and check it at the end
Move the machine to another outlet and keep going and check the fuse later
Run an extension lead from the nearest power point and tape it down across the floor

knowledgeChecks.question: Which electrical practice is unsafe with portable equipment?
options: Tagging out a faulty machine and reporting it
Checking the residual-current protection before use
Using a damaged lead while it still powers the machine
Arranging an authorised inspection

knowledgeChecks.question: What must be recorded and tagged before faulty equipment is reused?
options: Record and tag out the fault, and arrange an authorised inspection before reuse
Note it only in your memory and tell the crew at lunch and at the end of the day
Nothing, if it works after a reset and the reset is recorded on the wall
Keep the fault unlogged so the next worker is not worried and the machine is kept in use
